usage: xo mod tidy [--dir=<dir>] [--json]
       xo mod graph [--dir=<dir>] [--json]
       xo mod accept-effects [--dir=<dir>] [--json] [<module path>...]
       xo mod clean
       xo mod proxy serve [--addr=127.0.0.1:7070] [--fetch] [<cache dir>]
       xo mod proxy fill --to=<bucket URL> [--region=auto] <module path>[@version]...
       xo mod sumdb keygen <log name> <key file>
       xo mod sumdb serve --key=<key file> [--addr=127.0.0.1:7071] [--fetch] [--copy-to=<bucket URL>] [--fill-to=<bucket URL>] [--refresh=30m] [--rate=60] <data dir>
       xo mod sumdb restore --from=<bucket URL> <data dir>

tidy requires every imported module, drops requirements nothing imports,
and rewrites xo.lock with exactly the hashes the build uses.
graph prints the requirement graph as `go mod graph` does, one
"<module>[@version] <module>@<version>" edge per line (the main module
without a version); --json adds the version selected for each module.
accept-effects records the current effects of the named modules (all
when none is named) in xo.lock (decision 0156). clean removes the module
cache. proxy serve serves a module cache read only over the module proxy
protocol (decision 0126); --fetch fills it from git on a miss.
proxy fill fetches each version from git (checked against XO_SUMDB's
log) and writes its .zip, .lock and .mod, then the module's @v/list,
into an S3-compatible bucket (path style, https://<endpoint>/<bucket>)
that serves the proxy protocol as static files (decision 0568); the
credentials are XO_FILL_ACCESS_KEY_ID and XO_FILL_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
sumdb keygen writes a new checksum log key to the file and prints the
key clients name in XO_SUMDB; sumdb serve runs a checksum log (decision
0124) with its records in <data dir>; --fetch adds a version the log
lacks from git, at most --rate a minute per client; --copy-to copies
each new record to a bucket before adding it, --fill-to writes each
version it adds to a proxy bucket as proxy fill does, and sumdb restore rebuilds
a data directory from those copies. GET /index?since=<RFC 3339 time>
lists the records added since, as JSON lines. --refresh rewrites every
module's @v/list in the --fill-to bucket from its tags on that interval,
and GET /refresh/<module path> rewrites one at once (counted in --rate).
